description:
## Why

Before writing code, settle which OSCAL models the workspace touches and which it explicitly does NOT. This bounds the scope of the alignment and informs the binding-choice decision in PKIX-9vnx.2.

## What

Document, in a checked-in `OSCAL.md` or similar (in the workspace root or pkix-lint/), the OSCAL model touch surface:

**Models we DO use:**

- Catalog (lint rule definitions — pkix-lint authors PKIX-domain Catalogs)
- Profile (lint bundle composition — `cabf.br.tls` as a Profile selecting from Catalogs)
- Assessment Results (lint execution outputs)
- Finding (per-finding records inside Assessment Results)
- Observation (raw evidence underlying a Finding)
- Risk (with status=deviation-approved — replaces bespoke Deviation)

**Models we minimally touch / pass-through:**

- Assessment Plan (referenced from Assessment Results' `import-ap`; we emit a minimal stub or accept caller-supplied reference)

**Models we DO NOT use:**

- Component Definition (system-component-implements-control mapping — out of scope; we're a validator, not a system inventory)
- System Security Plan (full system documentation — out of scope)
- POA&M (plan of action — may revisit if there's downstream demand)

## Acceptance

- [ ] Document committed to repo with the breakdown above plus per-model rationale.
- [ ] Cross-references to NIST OSCAL model JSON Schema versions targeted (pin to a specific OSCAL release, e.g. v1.1.2).
- [ ] Foundation for PKIX-9vnx.2 (binding choice) — i.e., the audit tells us how much of OSCAL the binding needs to cover.

## Out of scope

- Actually implementing the bindings or types — that's .2 and onward.

## Depends on

None (audit is the entry point).
title: OSCAL model coverage audit: which models we use, which Rust types map to each
